Subject: Pricing framework for multi-year commitment

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the product walk-through yesterday. Catalytic is enthusiastic about Redwood’s latency/cost profile for inference; we can move fast if we can lock a predictable unit rate for the first 18 months of a three-year commitment.

Quick ask: we are asking for a bounded "rate window" carveout — essentially a maximum delta on per-token price during year 1–2 so our CFO can model patient contracts. We realize this is nonstandard, so we wanted to surface it early and see what flexibility you have.

High level: 3 year commitment, $1.2M ARR commit in year 1–2 ramp, with potential for a 30% volume uplift year 3. Looking for: a 15% max price increase cap on per-token unit for first 18 months, plus predictable true-up cadence.

Can you point me to the internal owner for commercial exceptions and next steps for VP/CFO sign-off?

—Ariel

- Confirmed commit cadence (monthly vs quarterly true-up). If they insist on monthly, our finance team needs additional cash flow modeling.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing framework for multi-year commitment — request for carveout evaluation

Team — I ran preliminary margin sensitivity with Finance and Product. Recommendation to present to Naomi: approve a conditional, timeboxed rate-window carveout with the following details: 

1) Price-cap: up to +15% per-token for months 1–18 relative to initial contracted rate.
2) Exposure guardrails: cumulative vendor true-up exposure capped at 8% of committed ARR over the 18-month period; any excess to be absorbed by product margin reserve.
3) Floors & cadence: commit floor set to 90% of monthly committed tokens; true-ups quarterly (finance prefers quarterly to limit operational churn).
4) Visibility: grant read-only access to a subset of telemetry + monthly usage export; no SLA changes.
5) Exit: if usage falls below 70% of committed run-rate for two consecutive quarters, Redwood reserves right to reprice or terminate.

If Naomi is comfortable with these guardrails I propose we offer Catalytic a clean term sheet and attach the exception memo for signature. This preserves our economics while giving them predictability.

Karthik
VP, Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rate_window_sensitivity_v1.pdf

Subject: Exec memo: Catalytic Health — request for VP/CFO sign-off on limited rate-window carveout

Naomi — please see the proposed exception memo below. We are requesting VP/CFO sign-off to permit a limited, timeboxed "rate-window" carveout for Catalytic Health to close the deal within their procurement window.

Summary (one line): Approve a conditional 15% price cap for months 1–18 with strict exposure guardrails (cumulative cap 8% of committed ARR), quarterly true-ups, and a 90% monthly consumption floor.

Business rationale: Catalytic is a high-value account in our health vertical with strong expansion potential and references that Redwood’s performance wins over competitors on latency/cost. This structure materially reduces procurement friction and is expected to accelerate contract signature within the quarter.

Material downside: limited retro exposure (modeled worst-case at ~6.5% of year-1 ARR under conservative adoption), operational cadence for true-ups, and increased contract complexity.

Requested decision: Naomi — please indicate approval or require exec escalation by EOD Monday. If approved, Marissa will sign the exception memo, and Jonas will issue a final term sheet to Catalytic.

Attachments: commercial_exception_memo_final.pdf, rate_window_analysis_20270722.xlsx
